newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Swedish Riksbank seen keeping repo flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Swedish Riksbank seen keeping repo flat.

text.p: The Swedish Riksbank is expected to leave its repurchase rate unchanged at 4.10 percent at its regular Tuesday repo tender, a Reuter poll of eleven analysts showed.
Of the analysts asked only one could see a possible cut, but he put the chances of such a move at less than 50-50.
"Chances are only somewhat lower than 50 percent," Keld Holm, economist at Lehman Brothers, said.
"The crown is the key to continued cuts. It is too weak and needs to move into the Riksbank's target range, which means below the 118 level on the TCW index."
The TCW index was at 121.15 on Monday.

The Riksbank has set an upper limit for the crown on a real TCW index of 118, which means about 119 nominally. Furthermore, the Riksbank has several times emphasised the importance of a stronger crown.
Most economists think the Riksbank will keep cutting the repo rate, but some say it has reached bottom.
Although the Riksbank has not cut rates since December 17, 1996, it brought the repo down to the current level of 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent at the beginning of 1996.
"Continued cuts are not needed for domestic demand," Katharina Hoyland at JP Morgan said.

"Growth is rebounding and we forecast that the repo rate will be held stable in the future even if the risk in the forecast is more towards a cut if you look at the impressive inflation development and the continued production gap."
The Riksbank will present its inflation report on March 20. Several of the economists see it as a good opportunity to cut the repo.
"I think the Riksbank needs more information that confirms a low inflation rate," said John Eriksen at analysis company IDEA.
"We forecast an inflation rate of less than one percent, that is below the Riksbank's inflation target."
The Riksbank's inflation target is one percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.
